facts.title: Dendrolagus lumholtzi (Lumholtz's tree kangaroo) | INFORMATION | Animal Diversity Web

There is a tendency among biologists and naturalists to concentrate research efforts on the cute-and-cuddly animals rather than the less pretty ones. With this pervasive doctrine you would think that we would know an awful lot about our appealing mammals. Well this is true for some species, but not for all. Tree-kangaroos are a specialised subgroup of the macropod marsupials, and are surprisingly more diverse in Papua New Guinea than in Australia. But irrespective of where they come from, our knowledge of even their most basic biology is still rudimentary.
